logs.name: _id
logs.desc: Internal ID for the log. This is guaranteed to always exist.

logs.name: _indextime
logs.desc: Timestamp when the log was ingested. This is guaranteed to always exist.

logs.name: _time
logs.desc: Timestamp found in the log, if present. If not present, will be set to _indextime.

logs.name: _raw
logs.desc: The original value of the log, verbatim. This is guaranteed to always exist.

logs.name: trace_id
logs.desc: If present, the ID of the trace that the log is a part of.

logs.name: span_id
logs.desc: If present, the ID of the trace's span that the log is a part of.

logs.name: trace_flags
logs.desc: If present, the flags of the trace that the log is a part of.

logs.name: severity_text
logs.desc: The level or severity detected in the log.

logs.name: severity_number
logs.desc: The level or severity number detected in the log.

logs.name: service_name
logs.desc: The name of the service that emitted the log. Derived from OpenTelemetry resources' semantic conventions.

logs.name: body
logs.desc: The body or main message of the log.

logs.name: _resource_fingerprint
logs.desc: A fingerprint that represents the resource that emitted the log. This is not guaranteed to be unique, but it should be unique enough within a reasonable duration for querying purpose. It is derived by hashing the key-values found in the resource, and so it is subject to hashing collisions.

logs.name: resource
logs.desc: The attributes of the resource that emitted the log.

logs.name: _scope_fingerprint
logs.desc: A fingerprint that represents the scope that emitted the log. This is not guaranteed to be unique, but it should be unique enough within a reasonable duration for querying purpose. It is derived by hashing the key-values found in the scope, and so it is subject to hashing collisions.

logs.name: scope
logs.desc: The attributes of the scope that emitted the log.

logs.name: scope.schema_url
logs.desc: The URL to the schema of the scope that emitted the log.

logs.name: scope.name
logs.desc: The name of the scope that emitted the log.

logs.name: scope.version
logs.desc: The version of the scope that emitted the log.

logs.name: _attributes_fingerprint
logs.desc: A fingerprint that represents the attributes in the log. This is not guaranteed to be unique, but it should be unique enough within a reasonable duration for querying purpose. It is derived by hashing the key-values found in the resource, and so it is subject to hashing collisions.

logs.name: attributes
logs.desc: The attributes of the log.

spans.name: _id
spans.desc: Internal ID for the span. This is guaranteed to always exist.

spans.name: _indextime
spans.desc: Timestamp when the span was ingested. This is guaranteed to always exist.

spans.name: _time
spans.desc: Timestamp found in the span, if present. If not present, will be set to __indextime.

spans.name: trace_id
spans.desc: The unique ID of the trace this span belongs to.

spans.name: span_id
spans.desc: The unique ID of a span within a trace.

spans.name: parent_span_id
spans.desc: The span ID of the parent of the span. Empty if no parent.

spans.name: name
spans.desc: Name of the span (the operation name).

spans.name: kind
spans.desc: Kind of span: INTERNAL, SERVER, CLIENT, PRODUCER or CONSUMER.

spans.name: service_name
spans.desc: Name of the service that emitted the span.

spans.name: resource
spans.desc: Key-values coming from the resource that emitted the span.

spans.name: _attributes_fingerprint
spans.desc: A fingerprint that represents the attributes in the span. This is not guaranteed to be unique, but it should be unique enough within a reasonable duration for querying purpose. It is derived by hashing the key-values found in the resource, and so it is subject to hashing collisions.

spans.name: attributes
spans.desc: Key-values assigned to the span by the instrumented code.

spans.name: events
spans.desc: A list of events that occured during the span's lifetime.

spans.name: links
spans.desc: Links to other spans that were relevant in the context when this span was emitted.

spans.name: scope
spans.desc: Information about the scope that emitted the span. Contains `version` and `name`.

spans.name: status
spans.desc: The status of the span. Contains `code` and `message`.

scalar.name: bin
scalar.desc: Categorizes input values into discrete bins based on specified binning criteria. For timestamps, the second argument specifies the duration of each bin, effectively rounding timestamps to the nearest interval. Returns the bin boundary containing the input value.

tabular.name: project-away
tabular.desc:
The project-away statement removes specified fields from the output.

Details:
- All fields except those specified will appear in the output
- Opposite of the project statement
- Useful when there are many fields to keep and few to remove
tabular.usage: Excludes specific fields from the results

tabular.name: project-keep
tabular.desc:
The project-keep statement keeps only the specified fields in the output.

Details:
- Functions similarly to the project statement
- More explicit naming for field inclusion
- Only the specified fields will appear in the output
tabular.usage: Keeps only specified fields in the results (similar to project)

tabular.name: extend
tabular.desc:
The extend statement adds calculated fields to the output without removing existing fields.

Details:
- Creates new fields based on expressions
- Keeps all existing fields in the output
- Can reference existing fields in the expressions
- Useful for data transformation and enrichment
tabular.usage: Adds computed columns to the results

extend with a scalar, with empty raw

tabular.name: distinct
tabular.desc:
The distinct statement removes duplicate rows from the results based on the values of specified fields.

Details:
- Returns only unique combinations of the specified fields
- Useful for finding all distinct values or categories in your data
- Can be used to deduplicate logs with the same values

tabular.name: count
tabular.desc:
The count statement returns the number of rows that match the query.

Details:
- Returns a single number representing the total count
- Can be used after other filter operations
- Simpler alternative to 'summarize count()'
tabular.usage: Returns the count of logs matching the query

tabular.name: sample
tabular.desc:
The sample statement returns a random sample of rows from the input.

Details:
- Useful for exploring large datasets
- Provides a representative subset of data
- Number specifies the maximum sample size
tabular.usage: Randomly samples a specified number of logs

tabular.name: sort
tabular.desc:
The sort statement orders the results based on values in specified fields.

Details:
- Default sort order is ascending
- Use 'desc' for descending sort order
- Can sort by multiple fields (secondary sort)
- Null values are considered smaller than non-null values

tabular.name: take
tabular.desc:
The take statement (also known as 'limit') restricts the number of rows returned.

Details:
- Returns at most the specified number of rows
- Often used with sort to get top/bottom N values
- Applied after all other operators in the pipeline
tabular.usage: Limits the number of rows returned

tabular.name: top
tabular.desc:
The top statement returns the first N rows when sorted by the specified fields.

Details:
- Default sort order is descending
- Combines sort and take in a single operation
- Useful for finding maximum or top-ranked values
tabular.usage: Returns top N rows sorted by specified fields

tabular.name: getschema
tabular.desc:
The getschema statement returns a list of columns and their types.

Details:
- Returns a list of column names and their types
- The columns depend on the pipeline so far. Projections, aggregations, will change the schema
- Useful to discover which columns and keys are available at a given point in a pipeline
tabular.usage: Returns the columns that are available at this point in the pipeline.

tabular.name: search
tabular.desc:
The search statement performs full-text search across log fields. Note that this operator is not yet implemented.

Details:
- Not currently implemented
- Will support free-text searching across log content
- Planned to support advanced text search capabilities
tabular.usage: Performs full-text search across log fields (not yet implemented)

tabular.name: render
tabular.desc:
The render operation defines how results are displayed in visualization contexts. It is not a regular tabular operator and can only appear at the end of a pipeline.

Details:
- Special operation that can only be used at the end of a pipeline
- <render-op> specifies how to visualize the results
- Currently only supports 'split' as a render operator
- Split creates multiple panels based on one or more specified fields
- Will support additional rendering options in the future
- Not a regular tabular operator
tabular.usage: Defines visualization options for query results
